content.synthesis:
Across the three coverage dimensions (identity, funding, hiring), Roberto Livi is a high-confidence instrument-science professional embedded in UC Berkeley SSL's Heliospheric Research group and Stuart Bale's lab network, with strong topical alignment to the lead record (electrostatic analyzers, plasma instrumentation, solar wind, magnetospheric physics). The evidence base is concentrated in three layers - mission staffing (ESCAPADE EESA-i Instrument Lead role), scholarly output (h-index 53 per Google Scholar; MAVEN / Parker Solar Probe / SPAN-I co-authorship), and alumni / institutional linkage (UTSA-SwRI PhD lineage; SSL People Directory entry).

A divergent signal appears in the title mapping: SSL's official page lists "Assistant Researcher", ResearchGate lists "Associate Researcher", and ESCAPADE lists "EESA-i Instrument Lead". This is consistent with the UC Academic Researcher series (Assistant, Associate, Full) where a person's external scholarly footprint may be self-reported at a higher step than their current classification - the SSL HR-maintained page should be treated as authoritative for current institutional title.

The clearest tension for the lead's question is between funding and hiring evidence: although Livi's topical mission footprint is rich (MAVEN, Parker Solar Probe via SPAN-I, ESCAPADE EESA-i), no publicly indexed competitive grant explicitly to Livi as PI/co-PI post-2024-01-01 was located. The dominant public funding figure ($80M ESCAPADE) is a program-level allocation to UC Berkeley SSL under PI Rob Lillis, not a personal grant. By the same logic, although multiple SSL Berkeley postings surfaced (2024 Specialist; May 2026 PSIE postdoc; an Assistant/Associate Researcher posting via DPS AAS), none name Livi as supervisor/PI. The strongest inferred connection is topical, not nominative.

The implication for decisions is practical: prospective PhD / postdoc / research-engineer inquiries should not rely on third-party aggregator listings naming Livi; routing should go through the SSL jobs hub (https://www.ssl.berkeley.edu/jobs), aprecruit.berkeley.edu, jobs.berkeley.edu, and direct outreach using Roberto Livi's documented institutional email rlivi@ssl.berkeley.edu, with explicit acknowledgement that public job postings naming him as supervisor were not located.
